findings.title: Public findMany() removed and return types changed without updating callers
findings.body: The PR deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, the only method in this class that executed a query, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a bare `Prisma.Sql` fragment. `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` also change from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`. Only two files are changed in this PR, so any other code in the repo that calls `findMany` or consumes the old where-input shape will fail to compile or behave differently. The description presents this as a test-only update to an already-converted service, so reviewers are not told about this breaking API change. Confirm there are no remaining callers, or update them in this PR.

findings.title: Org/team authorization fragments are top-level ORs without parentheses, unsafe to compose with AND
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` reduces to `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses (the team variant does the same at line 206), and `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns that string as-is. A caller that embeds the result in a larger predicate, such as `WHERE ${await service.getAuthorizationConditions()} AND "status" = 'ACCEPTED'`, is parsed as `(A) OR ((B) AND status)`, so every row matching A bypasses the caller's extra constraint. `getBaseConditions()` hides this today only because it wraps the result when a filter is present, and returns the bare OR when no filter is set. The integration tests at lines 296 and 333 of the test file assert the unwrapped text, which locks this shape in. The fragments should be wrapped in parentheses where they are built.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted while the memoization logic remains in the service
findings.body: The whole `describe("Caching")` block ("should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") is removed. The service still memoizes through `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, and this PR changes those cached types to `Prisma.sql`. Nothing in the PR explains the deletion, and no replacement test exists, so a regression in memoization (recomputing every call, or returning stale values) would not be caught.

findings.title: New empty-membership branch in team scope has no test coverage
findings.body: `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` now appends the user-membership branch only when `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0`. This replaces the earlier `userId: {in: []}` behavior with new control flow. No test covers a team with zero memberships, so the `false` branch and the resulting SQL (team-only condition, no trailing OR) are unverified. The same applies to the `userIdsFromOrg.length > 0` branch in the org scope when an org has no sub-teams.
